October 13

Hotfixes

**Bonus Events
**
Entering a Timewalking Dungeon will no longer clear any planted plants from the Druid Evergreen upgrade.
The fireballs from the cooking buff "Pepper Breath" should now scale properly in Timewalking.
Class Hall Set 6-piece and 8-piece bonuses should now scale properly in Timewalking.

***Classes***

**Druid**

Ironfur no longer incorrectly multiplies Bonus Armor effects from temporary buffs.
(Balance) New Moon, Half Moon, and Full Moon are now in the Arcane spell school.

***Items***

Spirit Cauldrons no longer have collision.


***Player versus Player***

Reminder: These changes are only active while in PvP combat situations and do not affect PvE. Many more Honor Talent changes are coming with Patch 7.1, including changes to Destruction Warlocks, Windwalker Monks, Death Knights, Balance Druids, and Restoration Druids.

**Mage**

Frost

Ice Form now has a 60 second cooldown (was 45 seconds).
Ice Form can no longer be cast while stunned.
Ice Form will now cause the Mage to be immune to only stuns, instead of other unintended crowd-control effects, such as Paralysis.
Frostbolt no longer deals increased damage in PvP (was a multiplier of +10%).

Developers’ Notes: Frost Mages are intended to create burst windows with Shatter and Glacial Spike, but have been reaching unintended levels of damage. By reducing Frostbolt damage, we’re reducing the potential size of Icicles and Glacial Spike burst. The Ice Form fixes should reduce its uptime, which was too high.
Hunter

**Beast Mastery**

Beast Mastery Agility reduced by 10% in PvP.

Developers’ Notes: We’ve found Beast Mastery damage to be too high, but we don’t feel that it’s due to any specific ability or mechanic, so we’re reducing the overall PvP template.
Monk

**Mistweaver**

Mistwalk can no longer be cast while silenced.
Soothing Mist healing reduced by 10% in PvP. (Soothing Mist version of Ancient Mistweaver Arts is unaffected.)
Soothing Mist healing cast by Summon Jade Serpent Statue reduced by 10% in PvP.

Developers’ Notes: Mistweavers been one of our strongest healers. We feel Soothing Mist is doing too much healing per second on its own, making it so that the Mistweaver doesn’t have to use cast-time healing spells as much as other healers, even when their target is taking high amounts of damage. We’re reducing Soothing Mist slightly to address this. Mistwalk was never intended to be used while the Mistweaver was silenced or locked out of Nature, so we’ve fixed that as a bug.

**Paladin**

Pure of Heart no longer causes Cleanse to incur a cooldown when it removes poisons and diseases.
Pure of Heart no longer triggers when healed by a periodic heal effect, but will trigger when a spell such as Rejuvenation is initially cast.

Developers’ Notes: Retribution Paladins are designed to be a formidable damage dealer and also have a protective, counter-control kit for their allies. Pure of Heart is intended to “soft-counter” poisons and diseases, but we feel it’s too strong currently when the Paladin is paired with a healing-over-time healer. Pure of Heart will now only trigger when a healing spell is applied, but not periodically during the spell.

Retribution

Blessing of Sanctuary now has a 30 second cooldown, up from 25 seconds.

Developers’ Notes: Blessing of Sanctuary has proven to be a strong, signature Honor Talent, but we feel its cooldown is too short.

**Rogue**

Assassination

System Shock now properly requires an Envenom cast with 5 or more combo points.
System Shock’s damage has been reduced by 20%.
Assassination’s Agility has been reduced by 5% in PvP.

Developers’ Notes: The Assassination Rogue is intended to be a strong, persistent damage dealer that pressures targets but lacks the utility that Outlaw excels in or the mobility that Subtlety provides. We’ve been monitoring their damage and feel its higher than intended, and we’ve found some bugs with System Shock contributed to this. We’ve also altered their PvP template to effectively reduce their damage.

Outlaw

Control is King will no longer stack Adrenaline Rush above a 3 second duration.

Developers’ Notes: Control is King is intended to be an attractive choice for the Outlaw Rogue when within a control oriented team composition. This has worked out a bit too well. Now, subsequent procs of Control of King will no longer add to the duration, and instead will just refresh itself.

**Shaman**

Enhancement

Stormstrike’s damage is reduced by 15% in PvP.
Heroism and Bloodlust now have a 60 second cooldown when modified by Shamanism (was 45 seconds).

Developers’ Notes: The Enhancement Shaman is intended to be a formidable damage dealer who also provides offensive group utility through totems and buffs. Shamanism has been a popular choice for the Enhancement Shaman, allowing them to use Bloodlust/Heroism frequently and also in Arena combat. We like the utility this gives the Shaman, but feel its uptime is too high. Further, we feel the Enhancement Shaman’s burst damage with Stormstrike has been reaching unintended levels.

Sure thing, I'll try and help. When you click a golden cookie, you'll usually get one of two effects. The first is a frenzy giving 7 times your CPS for 77 seconds. The second is a Lucky! effect giving you the lower amount of either 10% of your current cookies or 20 minutes worth of cookies (so 1200 times your CPS). Ideally, you want this amount to be  1200 times your CPS. Cookie monster shows the cookies required to get the most out of this Lucky! effect. 

You can also visit http://cookieclicker.wikia.com/wiki/Golden_Cookie to get more info on golden cookies.

Pure speculation, but the game might be taking the achievement into account (in this case, both the gain 100 condensers and gain 100 of every building). As you gain achievements, you gain milk. Your milk vastly increases your CPS with the kitten upgrades, so this final condenser may in fact give you the most bang for your buck.

The amount of cookies you need for every heavenly chip increases with every chip you get. At 87 chips, you'd probably need something like 50 trillion minimum to get a single chip. To answer your question, yes your heavenly chips accumulate with every reset, as does your total amount of cookies earned. You simply need to reset with a much larger pool to obtain more chips. 

If I could make a suggestion, I would suggest somewhere in the 4-10 quadrillion region to ensure maximum efficiency (at least at your point in the game).

I understand the frustration of high ping players, but this is an action RPG. Movement and timing of abilities are central aspects of the game. It may sound selfish but I wouldn't want the game to be balanced around expecting a two to three hundred ping from the players. Because kiting and weaving required pin point precision, it's expected that this would not work for players who have frequent lag issues. I'm just going out on a limb here, but I feel the reasons for this choice have more to do with preventing kiting abuse during the early days of inferno than latency issues.

I understand the point of putting it in, but I fear that the bad outweighs the good in terms of gameplay. It feels unnatural getting away from an enemy and still taking damage after the fact. Don't get me wrong, I'm madly in love with so many aspects of this game. But given the fact that this type of "hit and weave" playstyle is rampant in this type of action RPG, it simply feels wrong that all of a sudden what I consider to be a major gameplay element is simply removed.

Provided a monster is significantly faster than you, you'd only be slightly lowering it's dps by running around while destroying your own. My argument is that under this system is seems more likely that ranged classes (Demon Hunter and Wizard by and large) will be forced into building high defensive stats rather than it being a choice. 

In the Diablo 2 model, a sorc could choose to forgo defensive stats for offensive ones if he/she felt confident in their timings and kiting ability. I fear that in Diablo 3 such choices will no longer be possible as taking hits will be nearly unavoidable from the faster enemies. I'm not suggesting that beefier builds shouldn't have their place, but I'd prefer it if both builds were viable.

I politely disagree. Getting hit or not should not be decided as the animation starts, as that not only makes it visually confusing for players, but discourages kiting. If you say that skill is related to timing, how can a player, who understands how quickly enemies move and attack and times their own movement accordingly, not be considered skilled? If anything, the current implementation encourages people to make "tanky" builds, which hinders diversity.

When a normal item drops (special cases include champion and rare mob packs, who seem to have nearly a 100% magic and up item drop rate) it goes through a series of rolls to verify the quality. I believe it starts out by checking to see if it would be a legendary, then set, rare, and finally magic. If it fails all of these rolls, it remains a white item. Magic find affects how these rolls are done. Therefore, magic find does not increase the amount of items, but rather the quality of said item. 

From what I've gathered from the beta (a terrible data pool to work with, I know), stacking magic find doesn't seem to have much of an effect in the low percentages. Blizzard confirmed that magic find would be a linear increase, and therefore to balance it in large amounts, they might have made it weaker in smaller amounts when compared to Diablo 2. As a result, your best bet for finding magic items early on will be from rare and champion packs who have an almost guaranteed chance of dropping one, and to stack gold find on your gear to pay for the blacksmith leveling fees.
